I calculated the Q3 values and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. The same code reproduces all 10 of your Q2 reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Top customer segment by net sales | enterprise, 308,738,043 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 243 |
| c. Top product category by net sales | svc, 399,933,245 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u217@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 230 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 703,476 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -16.3% |

To reproduce the Q2 values, I had to read the data in two ways your definitions don't state:

- **Dates in Korean time:** all `ordered_at` timestamps are in UTC. I added 9 hours (Korean time) before assigning orders to the quarter and month. Without this shift, the Q2 numbers don't match.
- **Customers counted by email:** the `customers` table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails. I counted customers by email, ignoring case and spaces, rather than by customer ID (b, f).
- **Segment names:** the segment values have inconsistent capitalization and stray spaces (e.g. `SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `). I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping (a).

STATUS: DONE
